title: Remove Duplicates Keeping the Most Recent Record
description: The user_events table has duplicate (user_id, event_type) combinations. Keep only the **most recent event** for each (user_id, event_type) pair — deduplicate by retaining the row with the latest event_date.
solution_sql: SELECT user_id, event_type, event_date FROM (SELECT user_id, event_type, event_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, event_type ORDER BY event_date DESC) AS rn FROM user_events) ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY user_id, event_type

test_cases.description: 6 unique (user, event_type) pairs after deduplication. User 1 login→Feb 15, User 1 purchase→Feb 20, User 2 login→Jan 20, User 2 purchase→Jan 15, User 3 login→Jan 25, User 3 purchase→Feb 10.

hints: Use ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, event_type ORDER BY event_date DESC) to number rows within each (user, event_type) group — the latest event gets rn=1.
Wrap in a subquery and filter WHERE rn = 1 to keep only the most recent event per (user_id, event_type) combination.
explanation: ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by (user_id, event_type) and ordered by event_date DESC assigns rn=1 to the most recent row within each group. Filtering WHERE rn = 1 retains only the latest record. User 1 has 3 login events — only Feb 15 (most recent) survives. User 2 has 2 login events — Jan 20 survives. Six distinct (user, event_type) pairs remain after deduplication.
